title: Modern tidal interaction models for rapid binary population synthesis: II. Binary black hole formation, mergers, and spins
summary: We present predictions for the merger rates and effective spin ($χ_{\rm eff}$) distribution of binary black holes (BBHs) from isolated binary evolution, using a new self-consistent tidal dissipation implementation in the rapid binary population synthesis code COMPAS. Most of the first-born black holes (BHs) in our simulated merging BBHs are formed with zero spins, with the exception of BBHs formed from chemically homogeneous evolution. The spins of the second-born BHs with the new model depend significantly on the efficiency of tidal dissipation and mass transfer history, and crucially, are not always consistent with pre-supernova synchronization. High-$χ_{\rm eff}$ binaries preferentially merge at high redshift due to smaller binary separations at BBH formation and shorter coalescence times, thus rendering them largely inaccessible to current gravitational wave (GW) detectors. We expect the intrinsic spin distribution of merging BBHs formed from isolated evolution to be strongly biased toward low $χ_{\rm eff}$ with current detectors, with a third of systems having $χ_{\rm eff} < 0.05$ and only $\sim 3\%$ with $χ_{\rm eff}>0.5$. However, $χ_{\rm eff}$ will increase as GW detectors become sensitive to higher redshift sources, with up to $\sim 15\%$ of systems having $χ_{\rm eff}>0.5$.

AI.tldr: This paper uses updated tidal dissipation modeling in COMPAS to predict that merging binary black holes from isolated evolution mostly have low effective spins detectable today, but higher spin mergers exist at high redshift and will be more observable with future gravitational wave detectors.
AI.motivation: To improve predictions for merger rates and spin distributions of binary black holes from isolated binary evolution with a more realistic tidal dissipation model.
AI.method: Introduced a new self-consistent tidal dissipation implementation in the COMPAS binary population synthesis code and simulated merging binary black holes accounting for tidal effects and mass transfer histories.
AI.result: Most first-born BHs form with zero spin except in chemically homogeneous evolution; second-born BH spins vary strongly with tidal dissipation and mass transfer, deviating from pre-supernova synchronization assumptions; high effective spin binaries merge mostly at high redshift, thus are less detectable currently; observed spin distribution biased toward low effective spin with current detectors, but higher spins will be more detectable as detector sensitivity extends to higher redshift.
AI.conclusion: The spin distribution of merging binary black holes from isolated evolution is influenced by tidal dissipation and mass transfer; current gravitational wave detectors see a low effective spin bias, but future detectors will observe an increased fraction of high-spin systems from higher redshifts.

title: Signatures of $^{56}$Ni Mixing and Neutron-rich Ejecta in Supernovae
summary: Supernova lightcurves are often interpreted with one-zone radioactive-decay models that ignore a key variable that can affect interpretation and inferred parameters: the distribution of radioactive material. Using a multi-shell model, we explore the impact of $^{56}$Ni mixing in supernovae and r-process material in collapsars. Moving $^{56}$Ni outward reduces the overlying diffusion column, producing faster and brighter rises at fixed $M_{\rm Ni}$, $M_{\rm ej}$, and $E_{\rm k}$, and changes the tail through local gamma-ray leakage. A fast, bright rise is not, by itself, evidence for low ejecta mass or a requirement for engine power, with significant overlap between highly mixed and engine-powered lightcurves. One-zone fits to mixed bolometric light curves produce visually good fits but biased parameters. At fixed opacity, outward mixing is absorbed mainly by low inferred $M_{\rm ej}$ and high inferred $f_{\rm Ni}$, while $M_{\rm Ni}$ remains stable. If opacity is free, the fully mixed case is recovered with $κ^{\rm fit}/κ^{\rm input}\simeq0.24$. These shifts affect inferred explosion energies and progenitor mappings, and amplified in photometric fits. Exploring collapsar r-process enrichment, we find that the signature is not always a NIR excess and depends sensitively on the nickel-powered background, radial placement, angular distribution, and viewing angle of neutron-rich ejecta. In our setup, spherical models often show optical suppression and delayed colour evolution. Our disk-wind models suggest that fast-rising on-axis GRB-SNe are poor r-process targets for equatorially confined neutron-rich winds, and become constraining only if the r-process material reaches latitudes $\gtrsim 30^\circ$ from the equatorial plane.

AI.tldr: This study shows that radioactive material distribution critically affects supernova and collapsar light curves, causing parameter biases in simple models and complicating detection of r-process signatures due to geometric and angular dependencies.
AI.motivation: To investigate how the spatial distribution of radioactive elements within supernova and collapsar ejecta affects light curve shapes and the accuracy of inferred physical parameters, which are traditionally modeled with simplified one-zone assumptions.
AI.method: Implemented multi-shell light curve models incorporating variable $^{56}$Ni mixing distributions and r-process material placement, analyzing impacts on light curve features compared to conventional one-zone radioactive-decay models.
AI.result: Outward $^{56}$Ni mixing leads to faster, brighter rises and biases in inferred ejecta mass and nickel fraction when using one-zone models. r-process signatures vary with geometry and observer angle, with only specific configurations producing detectable effects, indicating complexities in identifying r-process enrichment in collapsars.
AI.conclusion: The distribution and mixing of radioactive material such as $^{56}$Ni significantly influence supernova and collapsar light curve interpretations, causing biases in parameter inference if conventional one-zone models are used. Multi-shell modeling reveals that outward mixing alters light curve features and affects derived ejecta masses and explosion energies. r-process signatures in collapsars depend strongly on geometry and viewing angle, complicating their observational identification.

title: First Results from the LSST Shadow Survey: The Restless Luminous Blue Variable AT2017des in the Virgo-Cluster Galaxy, NGC4532
summary: The Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) will start in late-summer 2026, revolutionizing transient astronomy. Here, we present the Dark Energy Camera (DECam) Shadow Survey, which is designed to maximize the science potential of LSST by shadowing LSST observations of local galaxy-cluster fields, producing a nightly cadence of these fields. The Shadow Survey will discover extremely young supernovae (SNe), SN precursors, as well as other explosive transients and exotic phenomena, helping to characterize such transients at unprecedented cadence and depth when combined with LSST. We describe our workflow, pipeline, public data releases, and candidate vetting. As an early result of Shadow, we present the fitful luminous blue variable (LBV) eruptions of AT2017des in the Virgo-Cluster galaxy NGC4532. AT2017des has short-timescale variability (of order 10 days), peaking at around $M_r=-12.5$mag, brighter than normal LBVs, and similar to the more extreme flaring of hot LBVs/SN impostors such as SN2000ch, AT2016blu, and the precursor activity of SN2009ip. Our spectral time-series reveals features typical of these hot LBVs and SN impostors/precursors. Combining our data with long-baseline photometry from additional observatories, we find that the peaks of the outbursts of AT2017des are getting brighter over time, with 2026 peak fluxes being up to 5 times greater than in 2023 and an average brightening of $\sim0.05$ mag yr$^{-1}$. The peaks of AT2017des are more luminous than those of most other LBVs, only being fainter than bright precursors such as SN2009ip, and extreme SN impostors such as AT2016blu. AT2017des may therefore be ``ramping up'' to a terminal explosion.

AI.tldr: The DECam Shadow Survey supports LSST by providing nightly observations of galaxy clusters to detect and characterize young supernovae and explosive transients. Early results highlight the unusual, increasingly bright eruptions of the luminous blue variable AT2017des, which may be approaching a terminal explosion.
AI.motivation: Maximize the science potential of the upcoming LSST by conducting a shadow survey focused on local galaxy-cluster fields to detect young supernovae and other transient phenomena.
AI.method: The Dark Energy Camera (DECam) Shadow Survey observes LSST fields nightly, using a dedicated workflow and data pipeline for transient detection, with public data releases and candidate vetting.
AI.result: Discovery and characterization of extremely young supernovae and exotic transients. As an early science result, the study identifies increasing luminosity and variability in the luminous blue variable (LBV) eruptions of AT2017des, suggesting it may be approaching a terminal explosion.
AI.conclusion: Shadow Survey combined with LSST observations provides unprecedented cadence and depth for studying transient phenomena, exemplified by the detailed monitoring of AT2017des, which exhibits unique brightening behavior indicating it may be ramping up to a supernova.

title: A Collapsar-Disk Origin for GW190814
summary: GW190814 was a remarkable gravitational-wave (GW) event: a merger between a 23 solar-mass black hole (BH) and a 2.6 solar-mass compact object, with an extreme mass ratio that is difficult to reproduce through standard isolated-binary or dynamical formation channels. Recent work has shown that neutrino-cooled collapsar disks can become gravitationally unstable and fragment, producing neutron stars (NSs) or low-mass BHs in orbit around the newly formed central BH. These fragments may subsequently interact, scatter, merge with one another, or inspiral into the central remnant. We propose that GW190814 originated from such a collapsar-disk fragment merging with the central BH. A key prediction of this scenario is a temporal association with a stripped-envelope supernova preceding the GW event, and we identify the Type Ib supernova candidate SN2019npv, which occurred inside the GW190814 credible volume approximately 60 days before coalescence, as a possible electromagnetic precursor. Although this delay is too long for a conventional kilonova counterpart, we show that three-body interactions among disk fragments can excite some compact objects to wide orbits and naturally produce merger delays of weeks to months. While GW190814 itself was not expected to produce detectable tidal-disruption-powered emission, future delayed mergers in this channel could generate luminous transients through either reprocessed kilonova heating or shocks driven as merger ejecta collide with the preceding supernova ejecta. Finally, treating SN2019npv as the host makes GW190814 a bright standard siren and yields H_0 = 70.5 (+9.2, -6.4) km/s/Mpc.

AI.tldr: GW190814's unusual merger likely came from a neutron star or low-mass black hole fragment in a collapsar disk merging with a central black hole, preceded by a supernova candidate SN2019npv, explaining its extreme mass ratio and enabling a novel measurement of the Hubble constant.
AI.motivation: The challenging mass ratio of GW190814's merger components is difficult to explain via standard formation channels, motivating exploration of alternative origins.
AI.method: The paper proposes a collapsar-disk fragmentation scenario where a neutron star or low-mass black hole fragment merges with a central black hole, supported by identifying a candidate supernova precursor and modeling three-body interactions causing merger delays.
AI.result: The scenario explains the extreme mass ratio and predicts a temporal association with a stripped-envelope supernova precursor, supported by the identification of SN2019npv within the credible volume and consistent timing; it suggests future mergers could produce detectable luminous transients and uses SN2019npv as a standard siren to estimate Hubble's constant.
AI.conclusion: GW190814 likely originated from a fragment formed via gravitational instability in a collapsar disk merging with a central black hole, with detectable electromagnetic precursors and implications for cosmology and transient astronomy.

title: Accurate modeling for 3$\times$2pt analyses in Roman and Rubin: a study of model approximations
summary: One of the pillars of modern cosmology is the use of galaxy imaging surveys to extract information from the large-scale structure. In recent surveys, this measurement is typically performed through a 3$\times$2pt analysis, which combines auto- and cross-correlations between galaxy density and galaxy weak lensing. In this paper, we carry out a systematic study of three modeling approximations commonly used in such analyses: 1) applying the Limber approximation, 2) neglecting redshift-space distortions, and 3) using less accurate models for the nonlinear matter power spectrum. We carry out the study in the context of the final data from two major Stage-IV galaxy imaging surveys: the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope's High Latitude Imaging Survey and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time. To do this, we first validate our modeling pipeline, implemented in the software package CoCoA, against an established code base, CCL. Next, we perform a simulated likelihood analysis to assess the impact of these approximations on the cosmological constraints. We find all three effects to be important; neglecting any of them can induce biases in cosmological constraints approaching or exceeding $1σ$, and exceeding $2σ$ for Rubin in several cases. Moreover, we explore how the lens-galaxy sample configuration and scale-cut choice can influence the constraints.

AI.tldr: This study evaluates the effects of three modeling approximations in 3×2pt galaxy survey analyses for upcoming Stage-IV data, finding they can bias cosmological constraints substantially, emphasizing the need for refined modeling to obtain reliable results.
AI.motivation: To systematically assess the impact of common modeling approximations on cosmological constraints derived from galaxy imaging surveys, ensuring the reliability of 3x2pt analyses for upcoming Stage-IV surveys.
AI.method: Validated the modeling pipeline in CoCoA against CCL, then performed simulated likelihood analyses incorporating three approximations: Limber approximation, neglect of redshift-space distortions, and use of less accurate nonlinear matter power spectrum models, applied to data forecasts from Roman Space Telescope's and Rubin Observatory's imaging surveys.
AI.result: Found that all three approximations significantly bias cosmological constraints, with biases approaching or exceeding 1σ and surpassing 2σ for the Rubin Observatory in some cases. Also identified that lens-galaxy sample configuration and scale cuts modify constraint robustness.
AI.conclusion: Commonly used modeling approximations in 3×2pt galaxy survey analyses can cause significant biases in cosmological parameter inference and thus should be treated carefully or improved in analyses of Stage-IV survey data to ensure accurate cosmological measurements.

title: Composition of Radiation-Driven Winds from Type I X-ray Bursts
summary: Recent NICER observations of photospheric radius expansion (PRE) X-ray bursts reveal absorption features consistent with photospheres enriched in intermediate-mass elements. These features may arise from radiation-driven winds that eject freshly synthesized nuclear ashes, offering a new probe of X-ray bursts and neutron star properties. Motivated by these observations, we use the MESA stellar evolution code to simulate PRE bursts from accretion through the hydrodynamic wind phase. We model a range of ignition depths for both pure helium and mixed hydrogen/helium accretion and explore several prescriptions for convection during burst rise. We find that the wind abundances depend sensitively on both ignition depth and convective treatment, including the efficiency of semiconvective mixing and the prescription used to define convective boundaries. Bursts igniting at column depths greater than or equal to 5 x 10^8 g cm^-2 produce ash-enriched winds, with ejecta ranging from intermediate-mass to iron-peak elements depending on ignition depth, accretion composition, and the treatment of convection.

AI.tldr: Simulations of PRE X-ray bursts with MESA show that wind composition, ranging from intermediate-mass to iron-peak elements, depends on ignition depth and convection, supporting NICER observations of nuclear ash ejecta from radiation-driven winds.
AI.motivation: NICER observations detected absorption features in photospheric radius expansion X-ray bursts suggesting enrichment of intermediate-mass elements in photospheres, potentially due to radiation-driven winds ejecting nuclear ashes. This motivates probing X-ray bursts and neutron star properties via simulation.
AI.method: Used the MESA stellar evolution code to simulate photospheric radius expansion bursts from accretion through hydrodynamic wind phase, modeling various ignition depths for pure helium and mixed hydrogen/helium accretion, and exploring different convection prescriptions during burst rise.
AI.result: Findings show wind abundances are highly sensitive to ignition depth and convective treatment, including semiconvective mixing efficiency and convective boundary definitions. Bursts igniting at column depths ≥5 x 10^8 g cm^-2 produce ash-enriched winds containing elements from intermediate-mass to iron-peak depending on conditions.
AI.conclusion: The composition of radiation-driven winds in PRE bursts is intricately linked to burst ignition depth and convective dynamics, confirming that ejecta can contain nuclear ashes and providing a novel observational probe for neutron star and burst properties.

title: GalSBI: Forward Modelling Galaxy Clustering and Population
summary: Forward modelling is a powerful approach for analyzing large-scale structure surveys. For this purpose, we extend the GalSBI framework to jointly model the galaxy population and clustering using an efficient subhalo abundance matching scheme based on optimal transport. We use simulation-based inference to constrain the model parameters by comparing UFig image simulations with DES Y3 imaging data. As a validation, we find that galaxy photometry and morphology agree well with multi-band imaging data of different depths, namely DES and HSC deep fields. Galaxy clustering for simulation and data is also in good agreement when comparing the angular power spectrum for different magnitude and color cuts. We further compare simulated redshift distributions against high-precision photometric redshifts in HSC deep field imaging of the COSMOS field. We find the redshift distributions across magnitude cuts to be similar to previous work, however with more realistic uncertainty modelling due to the addition of clustering contribution to sample variance. The agreement of the mean redshifts with data is very good, between $0.2σ$ and $1.6σ$ for different magnitude cuts, with sample variance being the dominant uncertainty contributor in bright samples ($<24$ mag) and subdominant compared to galaxy population model uncertainty in fainter samples. As a byproduct we measure the galaxy luminosity function and galaxy-halo connection, which are broadly consistent with existing literature. The updated GalSBI code and galaxy population model are publicly available. They enable accurate forward-modelled image simulations with realistic clustering, which can be used to model the effect of sample variance, source clustering, redshift distributions, and blending in large-scale-structure surveys. This makes GalSBI a powerful tool for the analysis of current and next-generation cosmological galaxy surveys.

AI.tldr: This paper enhances the GalSBI forward modelling framework to jointly model galaxy populations and clustering using advanced subhalo abundance matching and simulation-based inference, validated against DES and HSC data. The resulting tool produces realistic image simulations that improve modelling of sample variance and redshift distributions, supporting robust analysis of large-scale cosmological surveys.
AI.motivation: To improve the analysis of large-scale structure surveys by developing an accurate and efficient forward modelling framework that jointly models galaxy population and clustering.
AI.method: Extend the GalSBI framework using an optimal transport-based subhalo abundance matching scheme combined with simulation-based inference comparing UFig image simulations with DES Y3 imaging data; validate using multi-band imaging from DES and HSC deep fields, and compare clustering and redshift distributions with observational data.
AI.result: The model achieves good agreement with observed galaxy photometry, morphology, clustering, and redshift distributions including realistic uncertainty modelling; it accurately measures galaxy luminosity function and galaxy-halo connection consistent with literature; the updated GalSBI code is publicly released.
AI.conclusion: The extended GalSBI framework provides a powerful, validated forward modelling tool enabling realistic image simulations of galaxy clustering and population, effectively addressing sample variance, blending, and redshift uncertainties in large-scale structure surveys, thereby enhancing analysis capabilities for current and future cosmological surveys.

title: Indication for Decreasing Dispersion Measure in the Population of Repeating Fast Radio Bursts and Connection to Young Supernova Remnant Expansion
comment: 15 pages, 8 figures, and 2 tables. The third-round revision has been submitted to ApJ
summary: Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration, highly energetic radio transients of uncertain origin. Repeating FRBs provide an excellent population for investigating their nature, particularly through studies of parameter evolution. Out of the 63 repeaters monitored by CHIME, we select the 19 sources with more than ten detected bursts, and examine their long-term dispersion measure (DM) evolution. Seven sources show statistically significant DM evolution and are classified as the golden sample. Of these, five exhibit a decreasing DM trend and two shows an increasing trend. We then perform a binomial test under the null hypothesis that decreasing and increasing DM variation trends have equal probabilities. The current combined sample, including our golden sample and additional repeaters with reported DM change rate from the literature, gives a p-value of 0.033, supporting that decreasing DM trends are more common in the repeating FRB population. This statistical result is consistent with scenarios in that the local electron density around repeaters generally decreases with time, for example due to expansion of a young supernova remnant (SNR). Finally, within the SNR expansion model, we provide an illustrative estimate of the SNR contributions to the DM for different ejecta masses.

AI.tldr: Analysis of repeating FRBs shows a statistically significant trend of decreasing dispersion measure over time, likely due to expanding supernova remnants reducing local electron density.
AI.motivation: To investigate the nature of repeating Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs) by studying the evolution of their dispersion measure (DM) over time.
AI.method: Selection of 19 repeating FRB sources with more than ten detected bursts from CHIME; analysis of long-term DM evolution; classification of sources showing significant DM evolution; binomial statistical test comparing increasing vs. decreasing DM trends; interpretation within the supernova remnant (SNR) expansion model.
AI.result: Seven sources show statistically significant DM evolution, with five decreasing DM trends and two increasing; the combined sample analysis yields a p-value of 0.033 indicating decreasing DM trends are more common; consistent with decreasing local electron density due to SNR expansion; illustrative estimates of SNR contributions to DM for various ejecta masses provided.
AI.conclusion: Decreasing DM trends in repeating FRBs are statistically favored, supporting scenarios where local electron density declines over time, such as from young supernova remnant expansion, enhancing understanding of the FRB local environment evolution.

title: Cosmological constraints from the DESI DR1 Bispectrum Full-Shape and DR2 BAO
summary: We present cosmological constraints from the combination of DESI DR1 full-shape measurements, including for the LRG bispectrum, and DESI DR2 BAO data. The joint analysis accounts for cross-covariance using mocks, while ShapeFit compression mitigates prior volume effects that hinder beyond-$Λ$CDM analyses. In $Λ$CDM, the bispectrum (P+B) shifts $σ_8$ up by $1.1σ$ and $S_8$ by $1.2σ$, reducing their uncertainties by $26\%$ and $28\%$, respectively. For $w_0w_a$CDM, DESI-only analyses with the bispectrum shift dark energy parameters toward $Λ$CDM, staying consistent with a cosmological constant within $1σ$. Adding CMB creates a preference for evolving dark energy: DESI+CMB (P+B) shows a $2.8σ$ deviation from $Λ$CDM. Including DES-Dovekie supernovae alone reduces this to $1.6σ$, while the full combination DESI+CMB+DES-Dovekie gives $3.1σ$, driven primarily by the CMB. The bispectrum consistently weakens evidence for time-varying dark energy relative to power-spectrum-only analyses. The bispectrum also enhances sensitivity to massive neutrinos: in DESI-only analysis, the power-spectrum-only posterior for $\sum m_ν$ is consistent with zero, whereas adding the bispectrum yields a mean of $0.26\pm0.17$~eV and a $95\%$ upper limit of $0.57$~eV, shifting the peak into the positive region and agreeing with oscillation lower bounds. For modified gravity, the bispectrum further constrains $μ_0 = 0.12\pm0.49$ from DESI-only data, consistent with general relativity. Our analysis shows that accounting for cross-dataset covariances and avoiding prior volume effects yields robust constraints, with the bispectrum raising amplitude parameters and tightening their uncertainties.

AI.tldr: This paper combines DESI full-shape power spectrum and bispectrum data with BAO, CMB, and supernovae measurements, applying careful covariance modeling and compression techniques to improve constraints. The bispectrum tightens amplitude parameters (σ8, S8), shifts neutrino mass constraints positively, and moderates claims of evolving dark energy, resulting in robust cosmological parameter measurements consistent with ΛCDM and general relativity.
AI.motivation: To improve cosmological parameter constraints and investigate beyond-ΛCDM models by combining DESI full-shape and BAO measurements, including bispectrum data, while rigorously accounting for dataset cross-covariances and mitigating prior volume effects.
AI.method: Joint analysis of DESI DR1 full-shape (power spectrum and bispectrum) and DR2 BAO data using mocks to account for cross-covariances; application of ShapeFit compression to reduce prior volume biases; combined with CMB and supernova data for extended cosmological model testing.
AI.result: Bispectrum inclusion shifts and tightens amplitude parameters σ8 and S8 by ~1σ and reduces their uncertainties by ~26–28%. For dark energy parameters, bispectrum inclusion shifts results towards ΛCDM in DESI-only data, but combining with CMB data shows a 2.8σ deviation favoring evolving dark energy, slightly reduced when adding supernovae. The bispectrum improves neutrino mass sensitivity, shifting the posterior mean to 0.26±0.17 eV and yielding a 95% upper limit of 0.57 eV. Constraints on modified gravity parameter μ0 are consistent with general relativity. Overall, the bispectrum tightens constraints and raises amplitude parameters while ensuring robustness through proper covariance treatment.
AI.conclusion: Inclusion of bispectrum measurements in DESI analyses improves cosmological parameter constraints by raising amplitude-related parameters and tightening uncertainties, while providing consistent constraints on dark energy and modified gravity models. Proper treatment of cross-covariance and prior volume effects is essential for robust results, with bispectrum data showing reduced evidence for evolving dark energy compared to power spectrum alone and enhancing sensitivity to neutrino mass.

title: Deep Newtonian Afterglows: Theoretical Light Curves for Quasi-spherical Outflows
comment: 30 pages, 15 figures, 4 tables. Accepted in MNRAS
summary: We investigate late-time gamma-ray burst (GRB) afterglows produced by quasi-spherical outflows propagating into a stratified circumburst medium during the deep Newtonian phase. Sub-relativistic ejecta generated in compact binary mergers or core-collapse explosions naturally develop velocity structures, while additional energy injection from a long-lived central engine, through spin-down luminosity and/or fallback accretion, can substantially modify the afterglow evolution. We develop an analytical framework for synchrotron emission from decelerated ejecta components undergoing energy injection in a stratified environment. The model provides multiwavelength light curves and corresponding closure relations for the deep Newtonian regime. We apply this framework to the late-time multiwavelength observations of GRB 171205A. In addition, we constrain the physical properties of quasi-spherical outflows using observations of short GRBs associated with kilonova candidates, together with long-term radio upper limits obtained years after the burst in a broader GRB sample. Our results show that late-time observations can place meaningful constraints on the dynamics, energetics, and energy-injection history of sub-relativistic quasi-spherical outflows from GRB progenitors.

AI.tldr: This paper presents an analytical model for late-time GRB afterglows from quasi-spherical ejecta with energy injection, validated by observations, enabling constraints on outflow properties and central engine activity.
AI.motivation: To understand the late-time evolution of GRB afterglows produced by quasi-spherical outflows in stratified media and the impact of energy injection from central engines.
AI.method: Developing an analytical framework for synchrotron emission from decelerated ejecta with energy injection in a stratified environment, producing multiwavelength light curves and closure relations for the deep Newtonian phase.
AI.result: The framework successfully models late-time multiwavelength GRB afterglows, constraining physical properties of quasi-spherical outflows and their energetics and energy-injection histories using observational data including GRB 171205A and short GRBs with kilonova candidates.
AI.conclusion: Late-time afterglow observations are effective in constraining the dynamics and energy injection characteristics of sub-relativistic quasi-spherical outflows from GRB progenitors in stratified circumburst environments.

title: Probing Baryonic Feedback Effect with CSST Weak Lensing and Future FRB Measurements
summary: We explore the joint probe on the baryonic feedback effect using the weak lensing measurement from the upcoming Chinese Space-station Survey Telescope (CSST) photometric survey and the dispersion measure (DM) statistics of the fast radio bursts (FRBs) from next-generation radio telescopes, i.e., the Square Kilometre Array (SKA) and the Deep Synoptic Array (DSA-2000). By employing the baryonic halo model, we compute the matter, electron, and matter-electron power spectra, and generate mock data considering realistic noise and systematic effects based on the designs of the telescopes. These mock data are then analyzed using the Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method to investigate the parameter constraints. We find that CSST weak lensing alone can constrain the baryonic feedback parameter $\log_{10} T_{\text{AGN}}$ to an accuracy of $3.1\%$, with the sum of neutrino mass bound $\sum m_ν < 0.53\,\mathrm{eV}$. When performing the $3\times2$pt analysis, the inclusion of FRB DM measurements can significantly improve the precision of $\log_{10} T_{\text{AGN}}$ to $0.4\%$, and will lead to a better constraint on $\sum m_ν$ with an upper limit $< 0.47\,\mathrm{eV}$ by effectively breaking the degeneracy. Our results demonstrate that the joint observation of future FRB DM and weak lensing surveys is a powerful tool for probing the baryonic feedback effect, which is helpful in obtaining robust constraints on the neutrino mass and other important cosmological parameters.

AI.tldr: Combining CSST weak lensing with FRB dispersion measures from SKA and DSA-2000 markedly improves constraints on baryonic feedback and neutrino mass, demonstrating powerful synergy for future cosmological studies.
AI.motivation: To improve understanding of the baryonic feedback effect and enhance constraints on neutrino mass and cosmological parameters by combining different observational probes.
AI.method: Applied the baryonic halo model to compute relevant power spectra; generated mock data with realistic noise and systematics based on upcoming CSST, SKA, and DSA-2000 telescope designs; analyzed the data using MCMC for parameter estimation.
AI.result: CSST weak lensing alone constrains baryonic feedback parameter to 3.1% accuracy and neutrino mass sum to <0.53 eV; combining with FRB DM measurements improves baryonic feedback parameter constraint to 0.4% and neutrino mass sum upper limit to <0.47 eV by breaking degeneracies effectively.
AI.conclusion: Joint analysis of future FRB dispersion measure data and weak lensing surveys significantly enhances precision in probing baryonic feedback effects and yields tighter constraints on neutrino mass and cosmological parameters.

title: Detection of relativistic orbital deformation from improved timing of PSR J1757$-$1854
comment: 10 figures, 5 tables. Under review. Comments are welcome
summary: PSR~J1757$-$1854, a 21.5\,ms pulsar, is a highly relativistic double neutron star (DNS) system in a tight eccentric ($e = 0.61$) 4.4\,hr orbit. With extremely large gravitational wave luminosity and one of the fastest orbital decay rates of any known DNS system, it is ideal for testing general relativity (GR) in the strong-field regime. Here we present results from a high-precision timing campaign combining archival data from the Murriyang telescope and Green Bank Telescope (GBT) with new high-sensitivity observations from the MeerKAT radio telescope and additional observations from the GBT. The extended baseline and superior sensitivity of MeerKAT have yielded substantial improvements to previously measured post-Keplerian parameters by a factor of around $\sim2$ or more. We report the first detection of the relativistic angular deformation, $δ_θ$ in this system, making PSR~J1757$-$1854 only the third DNS system for which $δ_θ$ has been measured, achieved here in just 9 yrs compared to the decades of timing required for both the double pulsar and the Hulse-Taylor binary. We demonstrate how $δ_θ$ can be used to constrain the spin-orbit geometry of the system, ruling out two of the four geometric solutions previously identified, while remaining consistent with GR. We also evaluate higher-order contributions to the periastron advance $\dotω$, including the second post-Newtonian correction and the Lense-Thirring term, and show that these have a measurable systematic effect on the inferred total system mass. The observed orbital period derivative, $\dot{P}_\mathrm{b}$ remains consistent with the GR prediction for gravitational-wave damping across a wide range of plausible distances.

AI.tldr: Using high-precision timing data from multiple telescopes, researchers detected relativistic angular deformation in PSR J1757−1854, improving constraints on its spin-orbit geometry and confirming orbital decay consistent with general relativity.
AI.motivation: To test general relativity in the strong-field regime using a highly relativistic double neutron star system with an exceptionally fast orbital decay rate.
AI.method: High-precision timing campaign combining archival data from the Murriyang telescope and Green Bank Telescope with new high-sensitivity observations from MeerKAT and additional data from GBT, improving measurement accuracy of post-Keplerian parameters.
AI.result: First detection of relativistic angular deformation (δ_θ) in PSR J1757−1854, constraining spin-orbit geometry and ruling out two geometric models, higher-order effects on periastron advance were measured, and orbital period decay matched GR predictions.
AI.conclusion: PSR J1757−1854 provides a robust testbed for GR in strong gravity, with improved parameter measurements confirming GR predictions and enabling refined understanding of the system's geometry and relativistic effects.

title: Universal Fitting Formulae for the Peak Concentration of Dark Matter Halos
summary: The prediction of the structural properties of dark matter halos is crucial for studies in modern cosmology and galaxy formation. Utilizing a comprehensive suite of N-body simulations spanning diverse cosmologies and box sizes, we derive a universal halo concentration prescription aligned with the excursion set theory framework. The halo peak height parameter was revised to incorporate the linear growth factor at the halo formation epoch, enhancing its physical relevance to assembly history tracking. For fixed halo mass, we fitted the distributions of the halo concentration and revised peak height to lognormal functions to extract their peak values. We find that these peaks follow a universal, tight relation invariant to redshift, box size, initial power spectrum, and cosmology, exhibiting remarkably small scatter. In particular, the relation flattens systematically with increasing revised peak height, approaching an asymptotic value of 2.54, consistent with previous reports of a concentration floor. The fitting formula consistently describes both the mass-concentration and peak height-concentration relations, easily quantifying how these relations depend on redshift and cosmological parameters. This universal framework enables robust prediction of the most probable (peak) halo concentration using our fitting formula or theoretical/semi-analytical mass assembly histories. A software package for calculating peak concentrations is publicly available online.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a universal, redshift- and cosmology-invariant model for predicting dark matter halo concentrations using revised peak height parameters and N-body simulations, enabling precise characterization of halo structural properties with a publicly released software tool.
AI.motivation: To predict structural properties of dark matter halos accurately, which is essential for cosmology and galaxy formation studies.
AI.method: Used a comprehensive suite of N-body simulations across various cosmologies and box sizes; revised the halo peak height parameter by incorporating the linear growth factor at formation epoch; fitted halo concentration and revised peak height distributions to lognormal functions.
AI.result: Discovered a universal, tight relation between peak halo concentration and revised peak height that is invariant to redshift, box size, initial power spectrum, and cosmology with minimal scatter; relation flattens at high revised peak height approaching a concentration floor of 2.54; fitting formula effectively describes mass-concentration and peak height-concentration relations dependent on redshift and cosmology.
AI.conclusion: The derived universal halo concentration model provides a robust tool for predicting peak halo concentrations consistent with theoretical and semi-analytical mass assembly histories, facilitating improved cosmological analyses. A related software package has been made publicly available.

title: FAST Pulsar Database IV. Spike subpulses and quasi-periodic subpulses of 25 pulsars observed by FAST
summary: Fine structures of individual pulses can be detected when observations are conducted with a high time resolution and a great sensitivity. We examined pulsar data observed by the Five-hundred-metre Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST) with a time resolution of 49~{\textmu}s, and detected a large number of spike subpulses of 21 pulsars and quasi-periodic subpulses from 13 pulsars. These spike subpulses cannot be or are marginally resolved by the FAST observation time resolution, and are generally strongly linearly polarized, which may be primary emission elements of subpulses. For the quasi-periodic subpulses from 13 pulsars, we measured their characteristic periods, generally a few tenths of a millisecond, and examined their possible correlation with pulsar rotation period.

AI.tldr: Using FAST with high time resolution, this study identified spike subpulses in 21 pulsars and quasi-periodic subpulses in 13 pulsars, revealing fine temporal and polarization structures potentially linked to pulsar emission mechanisms.
AI.motivation: To detect and analyze fine structures of individual pulsar pulses using high time resolution and sensitivity observations.
AI.method: Analyzed pulsar data observed by FAST with 49 microseconds time resolution, focusing on detecting spike subpulses and quasi-periodic subpulses in multiple pulsars.
AI.result: Detected numerous spike subpulses from 21 pulsars, characterized by strong linear polarization and near time-resolution limits, and quasi-periodic subpulses from 13 pulsars with characteristic periods of a few tenths of a millisecond, with preliminary analysis of their correlation with pulsar rotation periods.
AI.conclusion: Spike subpulses likely represent primary emission elements due to their polarization and temporal characteristics; quasi-periodic subpulses have measurable periods possibly related to pulsar rotation.

title: Constant-Roll Inflation: Analytical Formulae for Power Spectrum and Implications for Induced Gravitational Waves
summary: Constant-roll inflation provides a simple and analytically tractable framework for describing transient departures from slow roll, including non-attractor phases that can enhance the primordial curvature perturbation on small scales. In this work, we investigate the curvature power spectrum generated in a slow-roll--constant-roll--slow-roll scenario, focusing on the positions and amplitudes of the two characteristic peaks associated with the two transitions. We show that, in the parameter range where both peaks are well separated and sufficiently pronounced, the underlying constant-roll parameters can be reconstructed from the peak positions and amplitudes without performing a brute-force parameter scan. In addition, we construct a smoothed analytic approximation to the power spectrum, designed for efficient estimates of scalar-induced gravitational waves and related phenomenological applications.

AI.tldr: This paper studies a slow-roll--constant-roll--slow-roll inflation model, showing how to extract constant-roll parameters from characteristic peaks in the curvature power spectrum and providing an analytic approximation for use in gravitational wave predictions.
AI.motivation: To provide an analytically tractable model capturing transient departures from slow-roll inflation, particularly non-attractor phases enhancing primordial curvature perturbations on small scales.
AI.method: Investigate the curvature power spectrum in a slow-roll--constant-roll--slow-roll inflationary scenario, analyzing peak positions and amplitudes to reconstruct constant-roll parameters and constructing a smoothed analytic approximation of the power spectrum.
AI.result: Demonstrated that constant-roll parameters can be directly inferred from characteristic peak features in the power spectrum without brute-force scanning and provided an analytic approximation useful for estimating scalar-induced gravitational waves and related phenomena.
AI.conclusion: The study offers a method to efficiently reconstruct constant-roll inflation parameters from the power spectrum features and an analytic formula to facilitate phenomenological analyses, advancing the understanding of transient inflationary dynamics and their observational signatures.

title: Radio eclipse of the slowest spinning Galactic-field spider pulsar PSR J1932+2121 and its X-ray emission prospect
comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables; accepted for publication in A&A
summary: PSR J1932$+$2121 is a newly discovered spider pulsar with a pronounced radio eclipse identified by the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST); it provides an ideal laboratory for studying the eclipse mechanism and high-energy emission from its intrabinary shock (IBS). By modeling the orbital-phase-dependent dispersion measure variations and flux profiles during the eclipse region with the wind interaction and IBS geometry, we constrain the system to a nearly edge-on inclination ($i_{\mathrm{o}} \simeq 88.55^{\circ}$) and a weak stellar wind from a low-mass main-sequence companion. Our analysis of the eclipse mechanism suggests that synchrotron absorption by nonthermal electrons can reproduce the observed flux variations with reasonable parameters for the eclipsing medium. We further predict the synchrotron emission from the IBS in PSR J1932$+$2121, showing that its X-ray flux, particularly near the inferior conjunction of the companion star, could be detectable with XMM/EPIC, EP/FXT, or eXTP/SFA and should exhibit double-peaked orbital modulation by Doppler boosting. These results provide a theoretical framework for understanding this system and for guiding future multiwavelength probes of spider pulsars.

AI.tldr: This paper models the eclipse behavior and high-energy emission of spider pulsar PSR J1932+2121, finding that synchrotron absorption causes the radio eclipses and predicting detectable X-ray emission modulated by the orbit.
AI.motivation: The motivation was to utilize the unique properties of the newly discovered spider pulsar PSR J1932+2121, with its pronounced radio eclipse, as an ideal laboratory to understand the eclipse mechanism and high-energy emission processes in intrabinary shocks of spider pulsar systems.
AI.method: The method involved modeling the orbital-phase-dependent dispersion measure variations and flux profiles during the eclipse region, utilizing wind interaction and intrabinary shock geometry to constrain system parameters and interpret the eclipse mechanism.
AI.result: The results include constraints on the system's inclination and companion wind strength, the identification of synchrotron absorption as the eclipse mechanism, and a prediction that the intrabinary shock's synchrotron X-ray emission should be observable with current and upcoming X-ray observatories, exhibiting double-peaked orbital modulation due to Doppler boosting.
AI.conclusion: The study concludes that the eclipse mechanism in PSR J1932+2121 is predominantly caused by synchrotron absorption by nonthermal electrons in the eclipsing medium, and the system is characterized by a nearly edge-on inclination and a weak stellar wind from its low-mass companion. The predicted synchrotron emission from the intrabinary shock should be detectable in X-rays, exhibiting distinctive orbital modulation.

title: Minimal Extensions of the $α$-Starobinsky Model: Reconciling ACT DR6 and Reheating Constraints
summary: The latest combined data from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) DR6, Planck, and DESI yields a scalar spectral index $n_s = 0.9743 \pm 0.0034$, which lies approximately $2σ$ above the prediction of the standard $α$-Starobinsky inflation model. To address this tension, we propose two minimal extensions that preserve the model's plateau structure and attractor properties: a multiplicative exponential modification and an additive polynomial deformation, both governed by a single small perturbative parameter $δ>0$. We analytically derive the slow-roll parameters and inflationary observables up to second order in $δ$ and integrate them with reheating dynamics via the consistency equation. It is shown that the $δ$ term effectively shifts $n_s$ into the $1σ$ confidence region of the joint P-ACT-LB-BK18 dataset without violating the tensor-to-scalar ratio bound ($r < 0.038$). The viable parameter space at $1σ$ requires $α\lesssim 35$ with $δ\sim \mathcal{O}(10^{-2})$ for the exponential model, while the additive model requires $δ\sim \mathcal{O}(10^{-3})$ for $p=1$ and $δ\sim \mathcal{O}(10^{-4})$ for $p=2$. For the e-folding range $N_k \in [50, 65]$, the relevant reheating equation of state is $0<ω_{\mathrm{re}}\le1$. All viable scenarios yield a reheating temperature $T_{\mathrm{re}} \sim 10^9$ GeV, which is safely above the Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN) bound and below the gravitino overproduction limit.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes small perturbations to the $α$-Starobinsky inflation model to resolve its tension with recent cosmological data on the scalar spectral index, successfully aligning predictions with observations and satisfying reheating and tensor-to-scalar ratio constraints.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to address the tension between the latest cosmological observations of the scalar spectral index $n_s$ and the predictions of the standard $α$-Starobinsky inflation model.
AI.method: The paper proposes two minimal extensions to the $α$-Starobinsky model—a multiplicative exponential modification and an additive polynomial deformation, both with a small perturbative parameter $δ$. It analytically derives slow-roll parameters and inflationary observables to second order in $δ$ and incorporates reheating dynamics through the consistency equation.
AI.result: The $δ$ perturbation shifts the scalar spectral index $n_s$ into the 1σ confidence interval of joint observational datasets without violating the tensor-to-scalar ratio bound. Parameter constraints for viability are identified, with reheating temperatures consistent with cosmological bounds.
AI.conclusion: Small perturbative modifications to the $α$-Starobinsky model can reconcile its predictions with current cosmological data on the scalar spectral index while maintaining desirable inflationary features and reheating constraints.

title: EP251023a: A fast X-ray transient featuring a magnetar-powered optical internal plateau followed by a steep decay
summary: EP251023a is an extragalactic fast X-ray transient (eFXT) detected solely by EP without a gamma-ray counterpart. The prompt emission consists of a main emission with a duration $T_{90}=292\pm19$ s, followed by a long-lasting tail emission that persists until the observation ends at $T_0+1571$ s. With the upper limit of Konus--Wind, we derived a conservative upper limit on the isotropic gamma-ray energy $E_{γ,\rm{iso}}$ of $5.7 \times 10^{52}$ erg for the main emission phase. A redshift of $z = 2.232\pm0.001$ is identified from strong absorption features in the Keck spectrum, which also indicate a relatively low host-galaxy HI column density. Based on the broadband spectral energy distribution, the late-time light curves show an achromatic plateau, followed by an extremely steep decay with a slope of 3.99 after a break at about 49 ks, which is consistent with a rapidly spinning millisecond magnetar engine. Under the isotropic wind scenario, we obtain the initial period $P_0<2.27$~ms and the magnetic field strength $B_p<8.33\times10^{14}$~G for the magnetar; whereas considering a jet collimation with a typical opening angle of 0.1 rad relaxes these constraints to $P_0<32.15$~ms and $B_p<1.18\times10^{16}$~G. Together with GRB\,070707, EP251023a may represent a rare class of optical magnetar-powered internal plateaus with little external-shock contamination, unlike previous examples detected primarily in X-rays. Future discoveries of similar events will help clarify the relationship between magnetar-powered internal emission observed in the optical band and that detected only in X-rays.

AI.tldr: EP251023a is an extragalactic fast X-ray transient at redshift 2.232 showing a long emission tail and a late-time optical plateau with steep decay, consistent with a millisecond magnetar engine. Constraints on the magnetar's spin and magnetic field suggest a new class of optical magnetar-powered events distinct from primarily X-ray ones.
AI.motivation: To understand the nature and origin of the extragalactic fast X-ray transient EP251023a, which lacks a gamma-ray counterpart and exhibits unique emission characteristics.
AI.method: Multi-wavelength observations including X-ray, optical spectroscopy with Keck to obtain redshift and host galaxy properties, analysis of broadband spectral energy distribution and late-time light curves, and application of magnetar engine models under isotropic wind and jet collimation scenarios.
AI.result: Determined EP251023a occurred at redshift 2.232 with a low host HI column density, showed an achromatic plateau and steep decay consistent with a rapidly spinning millisecond magnetar, and constrained the magnetar's initial spin period and magnetic field strength under different emission geometry assumptions. The event likely represents a rare optical magnetar-powered internal plateau with little external shock influence.
AI.conclusion: EP251023a exemplifies a rare class of optical magnetar-powered internal plateaus distinct from those seen primarily in X-rays, providing new insights into the engine physics of such transients. Future similar event discoveries will enhance understanding of the connections between optical and X-ray magnetar-powered emissions.

title: CHEX-MATE: AMALGAM weak-lensing analysis of 41 Planck Sunyaev-Zel'dovich-selected galaxy clusters
comment: 33 pages (26 pages plus 7 pages of appendices), 17 figures, 7 tables
summary: We present a weak-lensing shear analysis of 41 Planck SZ-selected galaxy clusters at $0.11\le z\le 0.55$ from the CHEX-MATE sample, using wide-field Subaru/Suprime-Cam and CFHT/MegaPrime imaging from the AMALGAM project. We detect the azimuthally averaged weak-lensing signal around the X-ray peak of each cluster, achieving a median S/N of 6.5 per cluster. The $45^\circ$-rotated component has a median S/N of -0.1 and ranges from -1.8 to +1.8, consistent with zero. We model the excess surface mass density profile of each cluster with an NFW profile to infer weak-lensing mass and concentration constraints. The total systematic uncertainty in the weak-lensing mass calibration is assessed to be $8\%$. Using a hierarchical Bayesian framework, we then derive weak-lensing-calibrated scaling relations for the halo concentration, $c_{200}$, as a function of $M_{200}$ and redshift, and for the Planck SZ mass proxy, $M_{SZ}$, as a function of $M_{500}$ and redshift, while accounting for sample selection effects, weak-lensing modelling biases, and residual calibration uncertainty. At $M_{200}=10^{15}M_\odot$ and $z=0.25$, we find $c_{200}=3.53\pm0.71$ with an intrinsic scatter of $0.22\pm0.04$ dex. The inferred normalisation and scatter are consistent with recent $Λ$CDM predictions for massive haloes, with no significant mass or redshift dependence over the probed range. For the Planck mass proxy, our baseline regression yields $M_{SZ}/M_{500}=0.83\pm0.09$ at $M_{500}=7\times10^{14}M_\odot$ and $z=0.25$, with an intrinsic scatter of $0.10\pm0.02$ dex. A restricted model with fixed unit mass slope and no redshift evolution gives $1-b=0.72\pm0.11$. We also provide weak-lensing-calibrated posterior estimates of $M_{500}$ for the sample based on the baseline $M_{SZ}$--$M_{500}$--$z$ relation. These results provide an initial weak-lensing mass calibration for CHEX-MATE multi-probe cluster studies.

AI.tldr: Weak-lensing analysis of 41 Planck SZ-selected clusters yields calibrated halo concentration and mass scaling relations consistent with ΛCDM, providing a key mass calibration for cluster studies with controlled systematics.
AI.motivation: To calibrate the masses of galaxy clusters selected via Planck SZ effect using weak-lensing measurements, enabling accurate scaling relations crucial for cosmological and astrophysical analyses.
AI.method: Weak-lensing shear analysis using Subaru/Suprime-Cam and CFHT/MegaPrime imaging, modelling mass profiles with NFW profiles, and applying a hierarchical Bayesian framework to derive scaling relations accounting for biases and uncertainties.
AI.result: Median weak-lensing signal detected for each cluster with S/N of 6.5, halo concentration at given mass and redshift consistent with theoretical predictions, mass proxy to mass ratio around 0.83 with quantified intrinsic scatter, and presentation of weak-lensing calibrated $M_{500}$ estimates for clusters.
AI.conclusion: The study provides a weak-lensing mass calibration for 41 Planck SZ-selected clusters, finding halo concentration and mass proxy scaling relations consistent with ΛCDM predictions, with no significant mass or redshift trends.

title: Asteroseismology of neutron stars with both hyperons and $Δ$ resonances
summary: Employing various relativistic energy density functionals for nucleon-nucleon interactions, we investigate the impact of hyperons and $Δ$ resonances on the frequencies of non-radial oscillations in neutron stars, where the universal coupling scheme is adopted for the $Δ$-meson couplings. It is found that the inclusion of $Δ$ resonances is essential for neutron stars to accommodate the recent mass and radius measurements of PSR J0030+0451, PSR J0740+6620, PSR J0437-4715, PSR J0614-3329, and HESS J1731-347. As $Δ$ resonances start to emerge in neutron stars' inner core, the $g$-mode oscillation energy becomes concentrated within the $Δ$-admixed region, leading to a sharp increase in the $g$-mode frequency. We also examine the $f$-mode and $p$-mode oscillations and find that the impact of $Δ$ resonances on these modes is less pronounced than the $g$-modes. The oscillation frequencies calculated in the Cowling approximation are then compared with those from full general relativity, confirming that the Cowling approximation introduces an error of approximately 20\% for the $f$-modes and within 10\% for the $g$-modes. The notable effect of $Δ$ resonances on neutron stars' $g$-mode frequencies holds important implications for probing the internal composition of neutron stars.

AI.tldr: This study shows that Δ resonances inside neutron stars notably increase g-mode oscillation frequencies, crucial for matching observations and probing internal star composition, with Cowling approximation errors quantified.
AI.motivation: To understand the effect of hyperons and Δ resonances on neutron star oscillations and reconcile theoretical models with recent mass and radius measurements of neutron stars.
AI.method: Using relativistic energy density functionals for nucleon-nucleon interactions with a universal coupling scheme for Δ-meson couplings, the study calculates non-radial oscillation frequencies (g-, f-, and p-modes) in neutron stars, comparing results from the Cowling approximation and full general relativity.
AI.result: Inclusion of Δ resonances is critical for matching observed neutron star mass-radius data. Δ resonances cause a concentration of g-mode oscillation energy in the core, sharply increasing g-mode frequencies, while f- and p-modes are less affected. The Cowling approximation yields errors of ~20% for f-modes and <10% for g-modes. These findings suggest g-mode frequencies as sensitive probes of neutron star interior composition.
AI.conclusion: Δ resonances significantly influence g-mode oscillation frequencies in neutron stars and are essential to accurately model observed neutron star properties, highlighting their importance in probing internal stellar composition.

title: Late-Time Oscillating Quintessence in Light of DESI
summary: Recent DESI baryon acoustic oscillation measurements, especially when combined with Type Ia supernova and CMB data, sharpen the case for possible low-redshift dynamics in the dark energy sector. We study a simple and physically transparent realization of such dynamics: a quintessence field that is Hubble frozen for most of cosmic history and starts to oscillate around its minimum recently (at a redshift $z\approx 0.1$). This late onset of oscillations can occur in a broad class of models where the quintessence potentials have a shallow slope away from the minimum and steepen near it. This class of models can improve the fit relative to $Λ$CDM, with $Δχ^2\simeq -9$, while remaining competitive with common phenomenological dark energy parameterizations with the same number of parameters. The preference is driven mainly by the background expansion history, and near the best-fit region the resonant growth of quintessence perturbations and the associated Integrated Sachs-Wolfe (ISW) contribution remain small. More precise low-redshift distance measurements, together with late-time probes such as the ISW effect and lensing, may help distinguish this oscillating quintessence scenario from other forms of late-time dark energy dynamics.

AI.tldr: A quintessence dark energy model with late-time oscillations improves fit to recent cosmological data compared to ΛCDM, providing a viable explanation for low-redshift dynamics in the dark energy sector.
AI.motivation: To explore the possibility of low-redshift dynamics in the dark energy sector suggested by recent baryon acoustic oscillation, supernova, and CMB data.
AI.method: Study of a quintessence field model that is Hubble frozen for most of cosmic history and begins oscillating around its minimum at low redshift (~0.1), specifically focusing on potentials with a shallow slope away from the minimum and steepening near it.
AI.result: This model improves the fit to observational data relative to the standard ΛCDM model by Δχ² ≈ -9 and remains competitive with other phenomenological dark energy parameterizations with similar parameter counts; the preference is driven by background expansion history with minimal impact from quintessence perturbations and ISW effects near best fit.
AI.conclusion: Oscillating quintessence models with late onset of oscillations provide a physically motivated and observationally viable alternative to ΛCDM that can explain low-redshift dark energy dynamics, and future precise low-redshift distance and late-time probes may distinguish this scenario from other dark energy models.

title: Magnetized Coulomb crystals in neutron star crusts
summary: We investigate the properties of magnetized Coulomb crystals in neutron star crusts using a fully three-dimensional geometry with periodic boundary conditions. The electron density profiles are fixed via the Thomas-Fermi approximation, and the nonuniform magnetic fields are treated with the equivalent magnetic charge method. The study focuses on Coulomb crystals composed of $^{12}$C at an ion number density $n_d = 10^{-9}\ \text{fm}^{-3}$, subjected to various external magnetic fields. Nuclei are described by a Gaussian wave function, where the width $b$ encapsulates the effects of zero-point ion vibrations and finite temperature. Our findings show that the crystal softens as $b$ increases. The Madelung constant $K_M$ fluctuates with the external magnetic field $B_{z0}$ at $B_{z0}\leq 3\times 10^{14}$ G. At higher field strengths, $K_M$ increases until $B_{z0} \approx 3\times 10^{15}$ G and then decreases. The body-centered cubic (BCC) lattice is slightly more stable than the face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice when $B_{z0} < 3\times 10^{15}$ G, whereas the FCC lattice may become more stable at larger $B_{z0}$. The elastic constants $c_{11}-c_{12}$ and $c_{44}$ are computed and tabulated, which grow with $B_{z0}$ for $3\times 10^{14}\ \mathrm{G}\lesssim B_{z0}\lesssim 2\times 10^{15}$ G and then decline toward zero as the field strength increases further. For $B_{z0}\gtrsim 10^{16}$ G, it becomes difficult to identify a stable lattice structure. These results provide valuable insights into the role of strong magnetic fields in shaping the properties of Coulomb crystals in compact stars.

AI.tldr: This study models Coulomb crystals in neutron star crusts under varying strong magnetic fields, revealing changes in lattice stability and elasticity that inform the physics of magnetized compact star interiors.
AI.motivation: To understand the influence of strong magnetic fields on the structural and elastic properties of Coulomb crystals in neutron star crusts.
AI.method: Using a fully three-dimensional geometry with periodic boundary conditions, electron densities fixed by the Thomas-Fermi approximation, and the equivalent magnetic charge method to treat nonuniform magnetic fields, with nuclei modeled by Gaussian wavefunctions incorporating zero-point vibrations and temperature effects.
AI.result: The crystal softens with increasing ion vibration width; Madelung constant varies non-monotonically with magnetic field strength; BCC lattice is more stable at lower fields while FCC may dominate at higher fields; elastic constants increase with moderate field strengths and decline at very high fields, with lattice stability becoming uncertain above 10^{16} G.
AI.conclusion: Strong magnetic fields significantly impact the stability, lattice configuration, and elastic properties of Coulomb crystals in neutron star crusts, highlighting nuanced transitions in crystal phases and mechanical behavior under extreme magnetic conditions.

title: Extragalactic test of General Relativity with time-delay gravitational lenses
summary: Strong gravitational lensing, a key prediction of General Relativity (GR), offers a unique environment for examining alternative modified gravity theories. In this Letter, we employ a model-independent approach to estimate the parameterized post-Newtonian parameter $γ_{\rm PPN}$ using the time-delay measurements from H0LiCOW strong lensing systems. To minimize potential biases from cosmological models in testing GR, we use Gaussian Process regression (GPR) to reconstruct angular diameter distances ($D_{\rm A}$) from the newest baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) measurements, provided by the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) DR2 data. Based on the reconstructed angular diameter distances and four H0LiCOW lenses, we directly estimate the post-Newtonian parameter $γ_{\rm PPN}=0.93^{+0.16}_{-0.17}$ and the sound horizon scale $r_{\rm d}=136.36^{+5.14}_{-3.20}~{\rm Mpc}$. This is the first simultaneous measurement of $γ_{\rm PPN}$ and $r_{\rm d}$ without any assumptions about the contents of the universe or the theory of gravity. In the new framework of distance ratio $D_{Δt}/D_{\rm l}$ which avoids the bias introduced by $r_{\rm d}$, the $γ_{\rm PPN}$ constraint can be further improved to $γ_{\rm PPN}=0.89^{+0.19}_{-0.15}$. Our results provide a direct test of GR at the extragalactic scale, which is well consistent with the prediction of GR within $1σ$.

AI.tldr: Using model-independent methods and new BAO data, this work measures the post-Newtonian parameter γ_PPN from strong lensing and finds it consistent with General Relativity, thereby testing gravity on extragalactic scales without cosmological biases.
AI.motivation: To test the validity of General Relativity at extragalactic scales using strong gravitational lensing, while minimizing biases from cosmological model assumptions.
AI.method: Applied a model-independent approach using Gaussian Process regression to reconstruct angular diameter distances from DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation data, then combined these with time-delay measurements from H0LiCOW strong lensing systems to estimate the post-Newtonian parameter γ_PPN and sound horizon scale r_d.
AI.result: Estimated γ_PPN=0.93^{+0.16}_{-0.17} and r_d=136.36^{+5.14}_{-3.20} Mpc, achieving the first simultaneous measurement of these parameters without cosmological or gravity theory assumptions. Using a distance ratio approach further refined γ_PPN constraint to 0.89^{+0.19}_{-0.15}. Results are in agreement with General Relativity within 1σ confidence level.
AI.conclusion: The study provides a direct, model-independent extragalactic test of General Relativity, confirming its predictions for the post-Newtonian parameter γ_PPN with no significant deviation detected.

title: Probing Merger Shocks in Galaxy Clusters in the SKA Era
comment: Published in Advancing Astrophysics with the SKAII(AASKAII), 2026 (arXiv:2606.20366). Report-no:AASKAII/ArpanPal01
summary: Galaxy cluster mergers represent the most energetic phenomena in the Universe since the Big Bang releasing gravitational potential energy of $\sim 10^{63-64}$ erg, injecting turbulence and driving shocks through the intracluster medium (ICM). These merger shocks can accelerate cosmic ray electrons and compress magnetic fields, sometimes producing Mpc-scale synchrotron radio structures known as radio relics. Radio relics are powerful tracers of merger dynamics, particle acceleration, and magnetic field evolution, yet fundamental questions about the underlying physics and their time evolution remain unresolved. In this chapter, we review the current understanding of cluster merger shocks and their radio signatures, presenting the observational evidence from the SKA pathfinders and precursors, linking radio relics to shocks alongside outstanding theoretical challenges. We also consider related shock-influenced phenomena: radio phoenices from revived fossil AGN plasma and Gently Re-Energised Tails. Further, we outline the directions of investigation using the sensitivities of the SKA-Low and Mid complemented with X-ray observations that will allow us to make significant progress in understanding the cluster merger shocks. Detailed studies of individual targets in continuum and polarization and studies of populations of relics using wide surveys will both provide insights to the micro-physics and cosmic evolution of merger shocks. We present SKAO capabilities across staged deployments starting from AA0.5 to AA4 and identify science verification targets that will illuminate the physics of cluster merger shocks in the SKA era

AI.tldr: This paper reviews the role of galaxy cluster merger shocks in producing radio relics, summarizes current observational and theoretical challenges, and outlines how SKA's capabilities will enable breakthroughs in understanding the physics and evolution of these shocks.
AI.motivation: Galaxy cluster mergers are highly energetic events that generate merger shocks, producing radio relics as tracers of particle acceleration and magnetic field evolution. Key physical mechanisms and time evolution of these phenomena remain unresolved, motivating the need for deeper observational and theoretical study.
AI.method: The paper reviews current observational evidence from SKA pathfinders and precursors, linking radio relics to merger shocks. It discusses related phenomena like radio phoenices and Gently Re-Energised Tails and outlines future research directions using SKA-Low and Mid sensitivities combined with X-ray observations. Detailed polarized continuum studies and wide surveys are proposed.
AI.result: The study identifies outstanding theoretical challenges and highlights how SKAO capabilities from initial to full deployment stages (AA0.5 to AA4) will facilitate progress. Science verification targets for the SKA era are presented to advance understanding of merger shock physics and evolution.
AI.conclusion: Combining high-sensitivity radio observations with X-ray data will significantly enhance understanding of the microphysics, cosmic evolution, and particle acceleration mechanisms in cluster merger shocks, with SKA playing a pivotal role.

title: The large scale structure probes of dark energy
comment: 20 pages, 1 figure, 1 table; A Brief Invited review for RAA (Research in Astronomy and Astrophysics), prepared for the Special Forum: "Dark Energy and the Hubble Constant Crisis" at the 28th Annual Conference of the China Association for Science and Technology
summary: We present a brief review on the large scale structure (LSS) probes of dark energy. We cover probes that directly constrain dark energy such as baryon acoustic oscillation, redshift space distortion, weak lensing and cluster number count. We also review auxiliary probes that mitigate systematics in dark energy constraints, such as the SZ effect to constrain baryonic effect and broadband galaxy clustering to calibrate photometric redshift. We demonstrate the synergy between these probes in delivering dark energy constraint of both high precision and high accuracy.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews multiple large scale structure probes of dark energy, showing how their combined use improves the precision and accuracy of dark energy measurements by reducing systematics.
AI.motivation: To improve the understanding and constraints of dark energy using large scale structure (LSS) probes.
AI.method: A review of various LSS probes including baryon acoustic oscillation, redshift space distortion, weak lensing, cluster number count, as well as auxiliary probes like the SZ effect and broadband galaxy clustering, highlighting their individual roles and synergy.
AI.result: Demonstration that combining multiple probes enhances the precision and accuracy of dark energy constraints by mitigating systematic errors.
AI.conclusion: Utilizing a combination of both direct and auxiliary LSS probes provides a comprehensive and effective approach to tightly constrain dark energy parameters.

title: Inflation in a nutshell: From basics to latest advances
summary: Inflation is an elegant paradigm for the very early Universe. It not only offers a simple solution to the flatness and horizon puzzles of the standard hot Big Bang model, but also generates quantum fluctuations that seed CMB anisotropies and the formation of large-scale structure. In particular, both the spatial flatness of the Universe and a nearly Gaussian, scale-invariant power spectrum of the curvature perturbation predicted by inflation have been confirmed by various observations. Recently, a larger spectral index of curvature perturbation is preferred when combining with ACT DR6, and particularly when further including the $H_0$ prior from SH0ES, and then the Starobinsky inflation model is disfavored at more than $95\%$ confidence level. Even though modified reheating histories and non-minimal couplings have been proposed to achieve a larger value of the spectral index, the model with higher-order curvature corrections to Starobinsky inflation offers a concise and well-motivated explanation.

AI.tldr: The paper addresses recent data favoring a larger spectral index that challenges the Starobinsky inflation model by introducing higher-order curvature corrections, resulting in a better fit to observations.
AI.motivation: To address the recent observational preference for a larger spectral index of curvature perturbation which disfavors the Starobinsky inflation model at high confidence levels.
AI.method: Incorporate higher-order curvature corrections into the Starobinsky inflation model to explain the larger spectral index while maintaining theoretical consistency.
AI.result: The modified Starobinsky model with higher-order curvature corrections provides a concise and well-motivated explanation for the observed larger spectral index, overcoming tensions with recent data including ACT DR6 and SH0ES H_0 priors.
AI.conclusion: Higher-order curvature corrections to the Starobinsky inflation model can reconcile the model with recent observational data favoring a larger spectral index of curvature perturbation, offering a viable and elegant inflationary scenario.

title: Measuring local primordial non-Gaussianity from the clustering of DESI DR1 LRGs and QSOs
summary: We report the first measurement of primordial non-Gaussianity (PNG), parameterized by $f_{\mathrm{NL}}$, in the configuration space two-point correlation function (2pcf). We employ simulation based modeling and a novel approach for the mitigation of imaging systematics. We apply this method to samples of luminous red galaxies (LRG) and quasars (QSO) observed by the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) during the first year of its observations (DR1). The observed 68\% CL interval on $f_{\mathrm{NL}}$ is $-3^{+22}_{-21}$ using LRGs, and $ 0^{+17}_{-16}$ using QSOs. The joint measurement yields $f_{\mathrm{NL}} = -3^{+12}_{-12}$ at $\ [68\%]$ CL. Our pipeline imposes a Gaussian prior on the value of $p$ (which defines the PNG bias via the Universality relation), with $p_{\rm LRG} = 1.0 \pm 0.1$ and $p_{\rm QSO} = 1.6\pm 0.1$. The observed constraining power of DESI tracers significantly exceeds that of previous large-scale structure (LSS) surveys, and encouragingly, approaches the sensitivity of CMB probes of PNG.

AI.tldr: This paper reports the first measurement of primordial non-Gaussianity parameter f_NL using configuration-space two-point correlation functions from DESI luminous red galaxies and quasars, achieving constraints comparable to CMB probes by mitigating imaging systematics and employing simulation-based modeling.
AI.motivation: To measure primordial non-Gaussianity (PNG) using large-scale structure data in configuration space, improving upon previous methods and systematics treatment.
AI.method: Simulation-based modeling of the two-point correlation function in configuration space combined with a novel mitigation approach for imaging systematics, applied to luminous red galaxy and quasar samples from DESI DR1; a Gaussian prior on PNG bias parameter p was imposed based on Universality relation.
AI.result: Measured 68% confidence intervals on the PNG parameter f_NL were -3^{+22}_{-21} for LRGs and 0^{+17}_{-16} for QSOs, with a joint constraint of f_NL = -3^{+12}_{-12}. The constraining power notably surpasses prior large-scale structure surveys and approaches cosmic microwave background sensitivity.
AI.conclusion: The study demonstrates the first configuration-space 2pcf-based PNG measurement with DESI data, yielding competitive constraints on f_NL that validate the approach and highlight DESI's potential to probe early universe physics with LSS tracers.

title: Exploring the Cosmic Dawn through the 21 cm Forest and High-redshift Radio Sources with the SKA
comment: Published in Advancing Astrophysics with the SKA II (AASKAII), 2026 (arXiv:2606.20366). Report-No:AASKAII/Cang01. Advancing Astrophysics with the SKA II (AASKAII) outlines the transformative scientific advances that will be enabled by the SKA telescopes
summary: The 21~cm forest, seen as absorption features in the spectra of distant radio sources, is produced by intervening neutral hydrogen and offers a direct probe of the neutral intergalactic medium during the epoch of reionization (EoR). Because it is sensitive to small-scale structure and gas temperature, it can constrain the thermal history of the early Universe and physics that affects structure formation. Detecting individual absorption lines is challenging, mainly because of their weakness and the scarcity of high-redshift radio-bright sources. Recent progress, however, has made 21~cm forest studies increasingly feasible: new statistical observables can improve sensitivity within realistic observing times, updated radio-source counts have revised expectations for suitable background quasars, and deep-learning methods can extract physical information more efficiently.
